title: Thomas Aquinas and scholasticism
summary: Thomas Aquinas, born around 1225 into a family whose castle stood at Roccasecca, joined the new Dominican order as a student in Naples. He studied in Paris and under Albert the Great in Cologne, then taught theology at the University of Paris. Drawing especially on Aristotle, he fused Greek philosophy with Christian theology in works such as the Summa contra gentiles and the Summa theologiae, models of the universities' scholastic method. He died in 1274; in 1879 Pope Leo XIII held him up as the model Christian philosopher.

uncertainty.note: Born between 1224 and 1226 at Roccasecca; died 7 March 1274 at Fossanova Abbey.
